title: Ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer codes
authors: Cathy Cheng, Nigel Higson, Danilo Polo Ojito, Emil Prodan
abstract: In this paper, we determine the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds of arbitrary dimensions and topological type. We introduce a $C^*$-algebraic framework in which the quantum spin algebra $\A$ is realized as the twisted group $C^*$-algebra of an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic structure. We establish a correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of $P$: Every Lagrangian extension of such a subgroup determines a $C^*$-diagonal of $\A$, whose Weyl groupoid encodes the dynamics through a continuous 1-cocycle. This realization yields an explicit family of extremal ground-states for every admissible Lagrangian model, together with their decomposition into sectors. When the sector space is $T_0$, this gives a complete characterization of the ground-state spaces. We also prove that every Lagrangian stabilizer model admits a unique frustration-free ground state with a spectral gap. Our framework applies in arbitrary dimension, including higher abelian quantum doubles, homological codes, and a broad class of stabilizer models.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive $C^*$-algebraic framework to classify the ground-state spaces of generalized stabilizer quantum codes on complex manifolds. By relating these models to isotropic subgroups within a Pauli module, the authors provide explicit characterizations of the ground states, including proving the existence of unique, gapped, frustration-free states for Lagrangian models.
main_problem: The paper determines the complete ground-state spaces for a broad class of generalized stabilizer quantum models.
main_result: It establishes a deep correspondence between stabilizer models and isotropic subgroups of a Pauli module, providing a complete characterization of the ground-state space, especially when the model is Lagrangian.
method: The methodology employs a sophisticated $C^*$-algebraic framework, realizing the quantum spin algebra as a twisted group $C^*$-algebra and using groupoid theory to encode dynamics via 1-cocycles.
model_or_system: The models are generalized stabilizer quantum models defined over CW-decompositions of non-compact manifolds. The underlying structure involves an infinite discrete Pauli module $P$ endowed with a symplectic form.
key_observables: Ground-state space ($	ext{GL}$), frustration-free ground states ($	ext{GF}_L$), and the logical algebra ($\mathcal{A}_{	ext{log}, L}$).
important_parameters: The structure depends on the choice of the isotropic subgroup $L$ and whether $L$ is Lagrangian.
main_assumptions: The analysis is primarily conducted in the non-compact case, relying on the symplectic pairing $\omega_k$ on the Pauli module $P_k$.

paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the $C^*$-algebraic framework and the correspondence between models and isotropic subgroups, proceeding to characterize the frustration-free ground states via the logical algebra, and concluding with specific applications to models like the Ising and color codes.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting topological structures (manifolds, groupoids) to the physical properties (ground states, spectral gaps) of quantum codes is highly relevant for understanding topological quantum computation.
